Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:10:1.hebrew: אמימר מתני - בהדיא הא דאמר ר' אלעזר: אין עושין את האמה בשביעית מפני שנראה כעודר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:10:1.english: Ameimar taught - Explicitly that which Rabbi Elazar said: “One may not make a water channel during the Sabbatical Year because it appears as if he is hoeing.”

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:11:1.hebrew: עושה אדם זבלו אוצר - שמכניס כל זבלו בשביעית בשדה, ולא אמרינן דנראה כמזבל שדהו בשביעית:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:11:1.english: A person may make his manure a storage heap - That he brings all his manure into the field during the Sabbatical Year, and we do not say that it appears as though he is fertilizing his field during the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:11:2.hebrew: עד שיעמיק שלשה טפחים - ומכניס הזבל לשם, דמוכחא מלתא דלא עביד כדי לזבל שדהו בשביעית:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:11:2.english: Unless he deepens [it] three handbreadths - And places the manure there, for it is evident that he is not doing [this] in order to fertilize his field during the Sabbatical [year].

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:11:3.hebrew: היה לו מעט זבל - באותה שדה קודם שביעית, מוסיף עליו זבל והולך בשביעית, ואין צריך להעמיק:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:11:3.english: [If] he had a small amount of manure - in that field before the Sabbatical Year, he may continue to add manure to it during the Sabbatical Year, and he does not need to deepen [it].

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:12:1.hebrew: רבי אלעזר אוסר - אפילו אם היה שם מעט זבל קודם שביעית, להוסיף עליו בשביעית:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:12:1.english: Rabbi Elazar prohibits - Even if there was a small amount of manure there prior to the Sabbatical Year, [he prohibits] adding to it during the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:12:2.hebrew: עד שיעמיק שלשה - או שיתן הזבל על הסלע שבשדה, דלא נראה כמזבל. והיכי שרי רבי אלעזר לחפור ולהעמיק בשביעית, ולא חייש לנראה כעודר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:12:2.english: Unless he deepens [it] three [handbreadths] - Or that he place the manure on a rock that is in the field, so that he does not appear as one who fertilizes [his field]. And how does Rabbi Elazar permit [one] to dig and deepen [the ground] during the Sabbatical year, and is not concerned that he appears as one who hoes?

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:13:1.hebrew: כגון שהעמיק - קודם לכן. כלומר, הא דאמר רבי אלעזר "עד שיעמיק" — לא אמר עד שיעמיק בשביעית, אלא שהיה עמוק קודם שביעית:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:13:1.english: Such as where he deepened [it] - Prior to this. That is to say, that which Rabbi Elazar said, "Unless he deepens [it]" — he did not say [that he may] deepen [it] during the Sabbatical [year], but rather that it was [already] deep before the Sabbatical [year].

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:13:2.hebrew: זבלו מוכיח עליו - כלומר, אע"ג דמעמיק בשביעית הוא נראה כעודר ואסור — הכא מותר, שהרי זבלו שמניח לשם מוכיח עליו דלא עביד משום עודר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:13:2.english: His manure is proof for him - That is to say, even though [by] deepening [it] during the Sabbatical year he appears as one who hoes and [it should be] forbidden, here it is permitted, as his manure that he places there proves concerning him that he is not doing [so] for the purpose of hoeing.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:14:1.hebrew: שאם היתה עמוקה טפח - כלומר, שלכתחילה היה שם אמת המים בת ששה טפחים, ונסתמה עד טפח — מעמידה עד ששה טפחים. כלומר, חוזר ומעמיק אותן חמשה טפחים שנסתמה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:14:1.english: That if it was a handbreadth deep - That is to say, initially there was a water channel six handbreadths [deep] there, and it became blocked up to [a depth of only] a handbreadth, he may restore it to six handbreadths; that is to say, he goes back and deepens those five handbreadths that became blocked.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:15:1.hebrew: חצי טפח על שלשה - אם היתה בתחלה בת שלשה טפחים, ונסתמה עד חצי טפח — דודאי אינו חוזר וחופר אותן שני טפחים ומחצה, אע"ג דהוי דומיא דהיתה עמוקה טפח ומעמידה על ו' טפחים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:15:1.english: Half a handbreadth to three [handbreadths] - If [the channel] was initially three handbreadths [deep] and became blocked up until [only] half a handbreadth [remained], [it is obvious] that he certainly does not go back and dig out those two and a half handbreadths, even though it is similar to [the case where] it was a handbreadth deep and he restores it to six handbreadths.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:15:2.hebrew: כיון דמעיקרא לא עברי בה מיא - כלומר, ודאי באמה בת שלשה טפחים לא עברי בה מיא שפיר — לא קודם לכן ולא עכשיו — הוי טירחא דלא צריך:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:15:2.english: Since originally water did not flow through it - That is to say, certainly in a channel of three handbreadths [in depth], water does not flow through it well — neither beforehand nor now — [and thus] it is an unnecessary exertion.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:15:3.hebrew: טפחיים על שנים עשר - דלכתחילה היתה של שנים עשר, ונסתמה עד שני טפחים — אסור להעמיק עוד עד י' טפחים על אותן שנים הראשונים, משום דהוי טירחא יתירא, דקא מעמיק כל כך, ולהגביה קרקעית הגומא למעלה מששה טפחים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:15:3.english: Two handbreadths to twelve - For [if] originally it was twelve [handbreadths deep], and it became clogged until [only] two handbreadths [remained] — it is forbidden to deepen [it] further, up to ten handbreadths in addition to those first two, because it is excessive exertion, since he deepens [it] so much, and [needs] to raise [the earth from] the bottom of the trench higher than six handbreadths.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:16:1.english: Two handbreadths by seven handbreadths - And it became blocked to [a depth of] two handbreadths:

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:16:2.english: What is [the halakha] - [Is it permitted] to deepen those five [handbreadths] that remain?

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:1:1.hebrew: שלופי - כשהירקות רצופין, נוטל מהן מבינתיים. לאוכלן — מותר; ליפותן — אסור, בשביל ליפותן — אותם שנשארים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:1:1.english: Pulling out - When the vegetables are crowded, one takes [some] of them from in between [the others]. [Doing so] in order to eat them is permitted; [doing so] in order to improve them is forbidden — [that is,] for the sake of improving them, [namely] those that remain.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:1:2.english: One who thins out - Pulls out among vines that are overly crowded together.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:1:3.hebrew: בשל עניים - בפאה, א"נ עוללות, שאין לו לא כתף ולא נטף:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:1:3.english: In [that of] the poor - In pe'ah, or alternatively, olelot, which have neither a shoulder nor a pendant.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:3:1.hebrew: בנכי - בורות תחת הגפנים וזיתים, ונותן בהם מים:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:3:1.english: Bankei - Pits beneath the grapevines and olive trees, and one puts water into them.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:3:2.hebrew: עוגיות - עגול סביב, כמו: "עג עוגה ועמד בתוכה" (תענית דף יט.). ובדידין נמי — הן גומות:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:3:2.english: Circular ditches [ugiyyot] - [A ditch that is] circular all around, like: "He drew a circle [ag uga] and stood within it" (Ta'anit 19a). And bedidin as well are pits.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:4:2.hebrew: למעבד בנכי - עוגיות. והיכי שרי? והא תנן: אין עושין עוגיות:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:4:2.english: To make bankei - Circular ditches. And how could he permit [this]? But didn’t we learn [in a mishna]: “One may not make circular ditches”?

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:4:3.hebrew: הא בחדתי - שמעולם לא היו שם עוגיות, אסור לעשות בחולו של מועד, דאיכא טירחא יתירא. אבל עתיקי, שכבר היו לו שם עוגיות ונסתמו — מותר לחזור ולחופרן בחולו של מועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:4:3.english: This [is] regarding new [ones] - Where there were never circular ditches there, it is forbidden to make [them] on the intermediate days of the Festival, as there is excessive exertion. But old [ones], where he already had circular ditches there and they became stopped up, it is permitted to go back and dig them out on the intermediate days of the Festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:6:1.hebrew: מפני שנראה כעודר - לצורך שביעית, שהרי חופר כעודר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:6:1.english: Because it appears as if he were hoeing - [This is said] with regard to the Sabbatical Year, for one who digs is like one who hoes.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:6:2.hebrew: שמכשיר אגפיה לזריעה - כשחופר האמה ומניח העפר שבאמה על שפת האמה, מתקן אגפיה לזריעה, דעביד לה ארעא רכיכא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:6:2.english: Because he prepares its banks for planting - When he digs the water channel and places the dirt that is in the channel onto the bank of the channel, he prepares its banks for planting, for he makes it soft soil.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:7:1.hebrew: דקא אתו מיא בתריה - דכי חפר באמה, אתו לאלתר מים בהדי חפירה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:7:1.english: Where water comes after him - That when he digs in the channel, water comes immediately along with the digging.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:7:2.hebrew: מ"ד מפני שמכשיר אגפיה לזריעה איכא - אע"ג דאתי מיא בתריה, דהא שדא ארעא רכיכא אגפי האמה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:7:2.english: The one who said: “Because he prepares its banks for planting, there is [a prohibition]” - Even though water comes after him, for he threw soft earth onto the banks of the water channel.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:7:3.hebrew: ומ"ד מפני שנראה כעודר ליכא - דהא אתי מיא, ובעודר ליכא מים, ולכך לא דמי לעודר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:7:3.english: And the one who said, “Because it appears as if he were hoeing, there is no [prohibition]” - For water comes, and in [the case of one who is] hoeing there is no water; therefore, it does not resemble [one who is] hoeing.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:8:1.hebrew: אלא - לעולם דלא אתו מיא בתריה, ואיכא בינייהו דשקיל ושדי לבראי — דחפיר באמה ושדי עפר לבראי, רחוק מאגפי אמה, דלא מכשיר אגפיה לזריעה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:8:1.english: Rather - Actually, [it is a case] where water does not come after him, and [the difference] between them is where he takes [the earth] and throws [it] outside — that he digs in the channel and throws earth outside, far from the banks of the channel, so that he does not prepare its banks for planting.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:8:2.english: [According to] the one who said, “Because he appears as if he were hoeing,” there is [a prohibition] - For behold, he is digging and water does not follow him.

Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:9:1.hebrew: בדוכתיה מנח ליה - דלא שדי ארעא לבראי, דלא עביד אלא מרכך ארעא. אבל הכא שדי לבראי, לכך לא דמי לעודר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 4b:9:1.english: He puts it down in its place - For he does not throw the earth outside, as he does nothing other than loosen the earth. But here, he throws [it] outside; therefore, it does not resemble one who hoes.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:13:1.hebrew: זבלו מוכיח עליו - דליכא למיחש להא, דמאן דחזי החפירה (. לא) חזי ליה לזבל שבחפירה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:13:1.english: "His manure is proof for him" - For there is no [need] to be concerned about this — that whoever sees the excavation will (not) see the manure that is in the excavation.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:1:1.hebrew: מדלין לירקות - ממקום עמוק קרי דילוי. ואע"ג דאיכא טירחא יתירא — בשביל לאכול התירו; אבל לייפות, אפילו ליכא טירחא — לא התירו:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:1:1.english: "One may draw for vegetables" - [Drawing water] from a deep place is called diluy [drawing]. And even though there is excessive exertion [involved], for the sake of eating [the vegetables] they permitted [it]; but to enhance [them], even where there is no exertion, they did not permit [it].

Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:1:2.hebrew: כך מידל בשל עניים - דכי אסר רחמנא ליקח עוללות, ה"מ בשעת בצירה, כדכתיב (דברים כ״ד:כ״א): ״כי תבצור כרמך לא תעולל״ — איסור עוללות עלייהו:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:1:2.english: "So he thins out [the vines] of the poor" - For when the Merciful One prohibited taking olelot, this applies [only] at the time of the harvest, as it is written: “When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean” (Deuteronomy 24:21) — [it is only then that] the prohibition of olelot [applies] to them.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:6:1.hebrew: מפני שמכשיר אגפיה לזריעה - ונראית חרישה ממש, שסבורין הרואין שלכך מתכוין. אי נמי, חשיב ליה עבודת קרקע ממש; ואע"ג שאינו מתכוין לכך — מיהו מלאכה היא. ואע"ג דאמר ר' שמעון: "דבר שאין מתכוין מותר" — הא אמרינן: מודה ר' שמעון בפסיק רישיה ולא ימות. ורבנן סברי: כיון דע"י שינוי עביד ליה — לאו מלאכה היא ומותר, דלא שמיה חרישה:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 4b:6:1.english: "Because he prepares its banks for planting" - And it appears like actual plowing, as onlookers think that this was his intention. Alternatively, he considers it actual working of the land; and even though he does not intend for this, nevertheless it is a [prohibited] labor. And even though Rabbi Shimon says that an unintentional act is permitted — behold, we say: Rabbi Shimon concedes in [a case of] pesik reishei velo yamut [an inevitable consequence]. And the Rabbis maintain: Since he performs it with a variation, it is not [considered] a labor and it is permitted, as it is not termed plowing.
